spec.title: Lazy loading N+1 scaling vs eager loading

steps.caption: Each user attribute access triggers a separate network order query.
Scaling records inflates lazy round trips into connection stalls.
Selecting all child orders via IN keeps database round trips bounded.
Compute round-trip time for 1000 entities assuming 3ms network ping.

left.whatIf:
def simulate_lazy_vs_eager(entity_count: int):
    # Lazy Loading: 1 query for parents + N queries for children
    lazy_queries = 1 + entity_count
    # Eager Loading (selectinload): 1 for parents + 1 for children
    eager_queries = 2
    return lazy_queries, eager_queries

lazy_50, eager_50 = simulate_lazy_vs_eager(50)
lazy_1000, eager_1000 = simulate_lazy_vs_eager(1000)

print("=== N+1 QUERY SCALING FORENSICS ===")
print(f"Dataset (50 records):    Lazy: {lazy_50} queries   | Eager: {eager_50} queries")
print(f"Dataset (1,000 records): Lazy: {lazy_1000} queries | Eager: {eager_1000} queries")
print(f"Query Multiplier:        {lazy_1000 // eager_1000}x query explosion under lazy loading")
print(f"Lazy RTT (3ms/query):  {lazy_1000 * 3} ms total")
print("Eager loading bounds database query count to constant O(1).")

entries.partTitle: SQLAlchemy Query Profiling with echo=True & EXPLAIN ANALYZE

steps.caption: Query echo logs expose repeating parameter filters in user lookups.
CI listeners assert fetching users triggers strictly 2 SQL queries.
Repeated per-user SELECT logs fail query budgets cleanly.
Simulate lazy load loop recording child queries so assert_query_limit flags.

CI listeners assert fetching users triggers strictly 2 SQL queries.
Repeated per-user SELECT logs fail query budgets cleanly.
Simulate lazy load loop recording child queries so assert_query_limit flags.
steps.whatIf:
class QueryProfiler:
    def __init__(self):
        self.captured_queries = []

    def record(self, sql, params=None):
        self.captured_queries.append({"sql": sql, "params": params})

    def assert_query_limit(self, max_queries=2):
        count = len(self.captured_queries)
        if count > max_queries:
            return False, f"REGRESSION: Executed {count} queries (Limit: {max_queries})"
        return True, f"PASSED: {count} queries within budget"

profiler = QueryProfiler()
# Simulate selectinload execution
profiler.record("SELECT id, name FROM users")
profiler.record("SELECT id, user_id, total FROM orders WHERE user_id IN (1, 2, 3)")

for n in range(1, 6):
    profiler.record(f"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = {n}")
ok, report = profiler.assert_query_limit(max_queries=2)

print("=== SQLALCHEMY QUERY PROFILER LAB ===")
print(f"Total Queries Recorded: {len(profiler.captured_queries)}")
print(f"Query Budget Result:    {ok}")
print(f"Profiler Audit:         {report}")
print("Automated query budget assertions verified.")

entries.partTitle: Eager Loading Query Execution Engine Implementation

steps.caption: Two-step selectinload loads collections cleanly without Cartesian bloat.
Modern SQLAlchemy prefers selectinload over legacy subqueryload queries.
Explicit IN batching avoids joinedload row duplication on collections.
Simulate joinedload flat join rows producing duplicate parent records.
Two-step selectinload loads collections cleanly without Cartesian bloat.
Modern SQLAlchemy prefers selectinload over legacy subqueryload queries.
Explicit IN batching avoids joinedload row duplication on collections.
Simulate joinedload flat join rows producing duplicate parent records.
steps.whatIf:
class EagerLoadingEngine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.users_db = [{ "id": 1, "name": "Alice" }, { "id": 2, "name": "Bob" }]
        self.orders_db = [
            { "id": 101, "user_id": 1, "amount": 45.0 },
            { "id": 102, "user_id": 1, "amount": 90.0 },
            { "id": 103, "user_id": 2, "amount": 15.0 }
        ]

    def execute_selectinload(self):
        # 1. Query users (Query 1)
        users = [dict(u) for u in self.users_db]
        uids = [u["id"] for u in users]
        # 2. Query orders with IN clause (Query 2)
        orders = [o for o in self.orders_db if o["user_id"] in uids]
        # 3. In-memory stitch (O(N))
        for u in users:
            u["orders"] = [o for o in orders if o["user_id"] == u["id"]]
        return users, 2

    def execute_joinedload(self):
        rows = [(u["name"], o["id"], o["amount"]) for u in self.users_db for o in self.orders_db if o["user_id"] == u["id"]]
        return rows, 1

engine = EagerLoadingEngine()
populated_users, query_count = engine.execute_selectinload()

print("=== EAGER LOADING ENGINE LAB ===")
print(f"Total Queries Executed:  {query_count}")
print(f"User 1 Order Count:      {len(populated_users[0]['orders'])}")
print(f"User 2 Order Count:      {len(populated_users[1]['orders'])}")
print(f"User 1 Order 1 Amount:   ${populated_users[0]['orders'][0]['amount']}")
flat_rows, j_queries = engine.execute_joinedload()
print(f"Joinedload ({j_queries} Query): {len(flat_rows)} duplicate parent rows -> {flat_rows}")
print("selectinload execution strategy successfully simulated.")

spec.title: Vendor reporting endpoint before and after SQL eager tuning

steps.caption: Lazy invoice traversal fires one thousand consecutive vendor queries.
Pushing aggregation into selectinload queries trims query count to 2.
Replacing loop queries eliminates reporting connection starvation.
Recalculate reporting benchmark with 10ms network ping showing 10s stall.

left.whatIf:
class ReportingOptimizationLab:
    def __init__(self):
        self.vendors_count = 1000
        self.avg_invoices_per_vendor = 5

    def benchmark_legacy_report(self):
        # 1 query for vendors + 1000 queries for invoices
        queries = 1 + self.vendors_count
        latency_ms = queries * 10.0
        return queries, latency_ms

    def benchmark_optimized_report(self):
        # 1 query for vendors + 1 selectinload query for invoices
        queries = 2
        latency_ms = queries * 4.5 + 13.0  # Network + in-memory sum
        return queries, latency_ms

lab = ReportingOptimizationLab()
leg_q, leg_lat = lab.benchmark_legacy_report()
opt_q, opt_lat = lab.benchmark_optimized_report()

print("=== ENTERPRISE REPORTING BENCHMARK ===")
print(f"Legacy Reporting Endpoint:    {leg_q} queries | {leg_lat:.1f} ms [TIMEOUT HAZARD]")
print(f"Optimized Reporting Endpoint: {opt_q} queries    | {opt_lat:.1f} ms [REMEDIATED]")
print(f"Latency Speedup:              {leg_lat / opt_lat:.1f}x faster execution")
print("Enterprise reporting query optimization verified.")

entries.partTitle: Full Eager Loading & Query Planner Synthesis Lab

steps.caption: Eager selectinload invariants block accidental runtime N+1 queries.
Keyset cursor pagination sustains bounded queries without OFFSET scans.
Planner hydrates all vendor invoices in 2 constant-count queries.
Run fetch_vendors_with_invoices with eager=True confirming constant queries.
Eager selectinload invariants block accidental runtime N+1 queries.
Keyset cursor pagination sustains bounded queries without OFFSET scans.
Planner hydrates all vendor invoices in 2 constant-count queries.
Run fetch_vendors_with_invoices with eager=True confirming constant queries.
steps.whatIf:
class RelationalQueryPlanner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stats = {"queries": 0, "records_loaded": 0}

    def fetch_vendors_with_invoices(self, vendor_ids, eager=True):
        if eager:
            # 2 Queries: 1 for vendors, 1 for all invoices
            self.stats["queries"] += 2
            self.stats["records_loaded"] += len(vendor_ids) * 3
            return f"Eager loaded {len(vendor_ids)} vendors and invoices in 2 queries"
        else:
            # N+1 Queries: 1 for vendors, N for invoices
            self.stats["queries"] += 1 + len(vendor_ids)
            self.stats["records_loaded"] += len(vendor_ids) * 3
            return f"Lazy loaded {len(vendor_ids)} vendors in {1 + len(vendor_ids)} queries"

planner = RelationalQueryPlanner()
res_eager = planner.fetch_vendors_with_invoices(list(range(1, 101)), eager=True)

print("=== QUERY PLANNER SYNTHESIS LAB ===")
print(f"Planner Execution:       {res_eager}")
print(f"Total Queries Emitted:   {planner.stats['queries']}")
print(f"Total Records Hydrated:  {planner.stats['records_loaded']}")
print("Complete query optimization and eager loading synthesis verified.")
